newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat condition shows slight improvement.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat condition shows slight improvement.

text.p: The condition of Oklahoma's wheat crop improved as western areas of the state received much-needed moisture during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.

Field activity slowed as wet, cloudy weather conditions persisted throughout the week. Flood damage from heavy rains was reported in parts of north central, central and eastern Oklahoma, where some wheat will have to be replanted.
Wheat was 97 percent emerged, compared to 95 percent a week ago, 86 percent a year ago and 88 percent on a five-year average.
Wheat rated 83 percent good to excellent, vs 81 at that level last week.
Sorghum harvested 86 percent vs 83 w/a, 90 y/a, 87 avg.
Soybeans harvested 90 percent vs 86 w/a, 89 y/a, 85 avg.
Cotton harvested 41 percent vs 35 w/a, 54 y/a, 68 avg.
Cotton rated 28 percent good/excellent, vs 28 last week.
Pasture and range condition rated 70 percent good to excellent vs 79 last week.
